We now have two df which contain all the epl (premier league) and ech 
(championship) game data. We can view the data below.

```{r Data frame heads}
head(ech_all)
head(epl_all)
```

We want to construct a filtration so as to remove any information we do not yet 
have access to so that we can prevent information leakage. We construct our new
training data frames below. The following is illustrative since we define 
functions to do same later on.

```{r Train df creation}
known_date <- as.Date("2025-01-19") # date upto which we have full information
cut_off <- 730 # a param used in time weighting, obvs this many days from known
               # date will have a weight of zero

train_ech <- ech_all %>%
  filter(Date < known_date) %>% 
  mutate(days_ago = as.numeric(known_date - Date)) %>%
  filter(days_ago < cut_off)

train_epl <- epl_all %>% 
  filter(Date < known_date) %>% 
  mutate(days_ago = as.numeric(known_date - Date)) %>%
  filter(days_ago < cut_off)
```

The training data sets can now be used to form team attack and defence ratings
for prediction. First we start of with our weighting function:

$$w(x) = \begin{cases}
1 - \left(\dfrac{x}{c}\right)^p, & 0 \le d < c,\\[6pt]
0, & d \ge c,
\end{cases}$$
where x is the days from obvs to known date, c is a cut-off, and p is a shape parameter.


```{r Weight function, echo=FALSE}
weight <- function(game_age, cut_off, power) {
  ifelse(game_age >= cut_off, 0, 1 - (game_age / cut_off)^power)}

library(ggplot2)
x_vals <- seq(0, 1000, by = 1)
power= 3.5
df <- data.frame(x = x_vals, y = ifelse(x_vals >= cut_off, 0, 1 - (x_vals / cut_off)^power) )

ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y))+
  geom_line()+
   labs(x = "Days ago", y = "Weighting", title = "Time decay of weighting") +
  theme_classic()
remove(df, power, x_vals)
```
In our weighting function we have a cut-off parameter which controls when we 
stop taking account of data, and a power parameter which controls the shape of 
the decay. A larger power parameter causes a greater period of high weighting, 
followed by a steeper decay to zero.

Now since we will create multiple training snapshots, we will define a function
to automate the creation of the training snapshot. We will also create a 
validation df which consists of games after the known date up to the end of some
validation window.

```{r Training snapshot func}
def_training_data <- function(data, known_date_, cut_off_, power_, validation_length_) {
  
  train_data <- data %>% 
    filter(!is.na(Date), Date < known_date_) %>% 
    mutate(days_ago = as.numeric(known_date_ - Date)) %>%
    filter(days_ago < cut_off_) %>%
    mutate(obvs_weight = weight(days_ago, power= power_, cut_off = cut_off_))
  
  validation_data <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(Date), Date >= known_date_) %>% 
    mutate(days_to = as.numeric(Date - known_date_ )) %>%
    filter(days_to <= validation_length_) 
    
  return(list(train = train_data, validation = validation_data))}
```

Let us use this function to create our first two training snapshots, we will
also extract our validation data at same time.

```{r Train snapshot creation example}
known_date <- as.Date("2025-01-19")
cut_off <- 730
weight_power <- 3

train_ech <- def_training_data(ech_all, known_date_ = known_date, cut_off_ = cut_off, power_ = weight_power, validation_length_ = 133)$train

validation_ech <- def_training_data(ech_all, known_date_ = known_date, cut_off_=cut_off,power_=weight_power, validation_length_=133)$validation

train_epl <- def_training_data(epl_all, known_date_ = known_date, cut_off_ = cut_off, power_ = weight_power,
                               validation_length_ = 133)$train

validation_epl <- def_training_data(epl_all, known_date_ = known_date,
                               cut_off_ = cut_off, power_ = weight_power,
                               validation_length_ = 133)$validation
```

Due to the way the dixon_coles adjuster works later on, we will label certain
data as for use by that model.

```{r Seperate DC data}
train_dc_epl <- train_epl
train_dc_ech <- train_ech
validation_dc_epl <- validation_epl
validation_dc_ech <- validation_ech
```

Now we have our basic training data, we will adjust it so as to give each team 
an unique row per game. This will allow us to use poisson regression on the home
and away teams realised scores. We create the function to create the goal data 
below. We will create a seperate function for the splitting of train and 
validataion data since validation data has no attached weights.

```{r Defining home_away split for goal data}
def_home_away_split_train <- function(data) {
home_data <- data %>%
  transmute(Date, Team = HomeTeam, Opponent = AwayTeam, Goals = FTHG, Home = 1, obvs_weight = obvs_weight)

away_data <- data %>%
  transmute(Date, Team = AwayTeam, Opponent = HomeTeam, Goals = FTAG, Home = 0, obvs_weight = obvs_weight)

train_goal_data <- bind_rows(home_data, away_data)

return(train_goal_data)}

def_home_away_split_validation <- function(data) {
home_data <- data %>%
  transmute(Date, Team = HomeTeam, Opponent = AwayTeam, Goals = FTHG, Home = 1)

away_data <- data %>%
  transmute(Date, Team = AwayTeam, Opponent = HomeTeam, Goals = FTAG, Home = 0)

validation_goal_data <- bind_rows(home_data, away_data)

return(validation_goal_data)}
```

We're now going to use our function to create our home away split goal data.

```{r training_goals_data gen}
train_ech_goals <- def_home_away_split_train(train_ech)
train_epl_goals <- def_home_away_split_train(train_epl)
```

## Section 2: Poisson regression model for team ratings

We are now going to fit a poisson regression model to obtain attack and defence
ratings for the teams observed in our train data. Note that it we will model the
scoreline for individual games under the dixon coles model. This models the home
and away goals as poisson random variables, with a correction term which adjusts
the probability of observing low-scoring scorelines. 

```{r fitting regression model to goals data}
ech_goal_model <- glm(
  Goals ~ Home + Team + Opponent,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  data = train_ech_goals,
  weights = obvs_weight)

epl_goal_model <- glm(
  Goals ~ Home + Team + Opponent,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  data = train_epl_goals,
  weights = obvs_weight)

summary(epl_goal_model)
summary(ech_goal_model)
```

We will now extract the attack and defence ratings as suggested by our 
regression model. The model uses reference levels for the team and opponent factors to ensure identifiability. We then centre the estimated log attack and defence effects and adjust the baseline accordingly. This produces ratings with geometric mean one while preserving the fitted expected goals.

```{r Extracting normalised ratings func}
extract_ratings <- function(model) {

  teams <- model$xlevels$Team
  coefs <- coef(model)
  
  # initialise each teams log_attack rating
  attack_log <- setNames(rep(0, length(teams)), teams)
  defence_log <- setNames(rep(0, length(teams)), teams)
  
  # now we extract ratings
  for (team in teams) {

    attack_name <- paste0("Team", team)
    defence_name <- paste0("Opponent", team)

    if (attack_name %in% names(coefs)) {     # since baseline team has no coefs,
      attack_log[team] <- coefs[attack_name]} # we only update teams with coefs

    if (defence_name %in% names(coefs)) {
      defence_log[team] <- coefs[defence_name]}}
  
  # center the log ratings so that prem and champ ratings can be scaled later
  mean_attack <- mean(attack_log)
  mean_defence <- mean(defence_log)

  ratings <- data.frame(team_names = teams,
    att_rating = exp(attack_log - mean_attack),
    def_rating = exp(defence_log - mean_defence))
  
  baseline <- unname(coefs["(Intercept)"]) + mean_attack + mean_defence
  home_advantage <- unname(coefs["Home"])
  
  return(list(ratings = ratings, baseline = baseline, 
              home_advantage = home_advantage))}
```

We implement the function below:

```{r Implementing our model}
epl_model <- extract_ratings(epl_goal_model)
ech_model <- extract_ratings(ech_goal_model)

epl_ratings <- epl_model$ratings
ech_ratings <- ech_model$ratings

epl_baseline <- epl_model$baseline
epl_home_advantage <- epl_model$home_advantage

ech_baseline <- ech_model$baseline
ech_home_advantage <- ech_model$home_advantage

head(epl_ratings)
```

Above we show the head of epl_ratings obtained by our poisson regression. These
ratings have geometric mean 1. That is an attack rating greater than 1 is given 
to a team who has a stronger attack, a defence rating below 1 is given to a team 
who has a stronger defence.

We will now see how these perform compared to our validation data. We will first
transform our raw validation data via the home away goal split.

```{r Validation home away goal split}
validation_ech <- def_home_away_split_validation(validation_ech)
validation_epl <- def_home_away_split_validation(validation_epl)
```

We use the predict function to give the number of goals we expect to see in our
validation data.

```{r Predict on validation data}
validation_epl$predicted_goals <- predict(
  epl_goal_model, newdata = validation_epl, type = "response")

validation_ech$predicted_goals <- predict(
  ech_goal_model, newdata = validation_ech, type = "response")
```

Now lets evaluate our model on the validation data. This is all for sanity check
to make sure our model is suggesting reasonable estimated goals.

```{r Sanity check evaluation}
evaluate_goals <- function(data) {
  errors <- data$Goals - data$predicted_goals

  data.frame(
    n = nrow(data),
    mean_actual = mean(data$Goals), mean_predicted = mean(data$predicted_goals),
    MAE = mean(abs(errors)), RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2)))}

```

```{r Baseline creation}
baseline_evaluate <- function(train_data, validation_data) {
  mean_train_goals <- mean(train_data$Goals)
  errors <- validation_data$Goals - mean_train_goals
  
  data.frame(
    baseline_mean = mean_train_goals, MAE = mean(abs(errors)), 
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2)))}
```

```{r Weighted mean baseline creation}
weighted_baseline_evaluate <- function(train_data, validation_data) {

  weighted_mean_train_goals <- weighted.mean(train_data$Goals, 
                                             w= train_data$obvs_weight)
  
  errors <- validation_data$Goals - weighted_mean_train_goals
  
  data.frame(
    baseline_mean = weighted_mean_train_goals, MAE = mean(abs(errors)), 
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2)))}
```

```{r poisson evaluation data table}
evaluation_results <- bind_rows(
  # Championship
  tibble(league = "Championship",
    method = "Weighted baseline",
    weighted_baseline_evaluate(train_ech_goals, validation_ech)),
  tibble(league = "Championship",method = "Unweighted baseline",baseline_evaluate(train_ech_goals, validation_ech)),
  tibble(league = "Championship",
    method = "Poisson model", evaluate_goals(validation_ech)),

  # Premier League
  tibble(league = "Premier League", method = "Weighted baseline",
    weighted_baseline_evaluate(train_epl_goals, validation_epl)), tibble(
    league = "Premier League",
    method = "Unweighted baseline",baseline_evaluate(train_epl_goals, 
                                                     validation_epl)),
  tibble(league = "Premier League", method = "Poisson model",
    evaluate_goals(validation_epl))) %>%
  select(league, method,MAE,RMSE)

evaluation_results
```
Okay so our poisson goals model seems to perform slightly better than our 
baseline estimate of just expecting to see the average number of goals from our
training data. We will now look to use a Dixon-Coles correction in order to 
improve the accuracy with which we predict the number of goals in a game.

We have a more indepth breakdown of the evaluation for our Poisson model below:
```{r echo=FALSE}
bind_rows(
  bind_cols(league="Championship",method="Poisson",evaluate_goals(validation_ech)),
  bind_cols(league="Premier League",method="Poisson",evaluate_goals(validation_epl)),
)
```
## Section 3: Dixon-Coles adjustment
We are going to use the attack and defence ratings from the fitted poisson model
in our dixon coles adjusted model for game out come (at least we will initially)
. Note that we should really fit these by maximising the likelihood of our 
observations under the dixon coles model. However, that would require us to 
maximise the custom likelihood function. We will aim to do this if testing for 
this model proves positive.

```{r Dixon-Coles adjuster}
dixon_coles_probs <- function(team_ratings, home_team, away_team, baseline, home_advantage, 
                              rho = -0.05, max_goals = 7) {

  # get team ratings
  home_att <- team_ratings$att_rating[team_ratings$team_names == home_team]
  
  home_def <- team_ratings$def_rating[team_ratings$team_names == home_team]

  away_att <- team_ratings$att_rating[team_ratings$team_names == away_team]
  
  away_def <- team_ratings$def_rating[team_ratings$team_names == away_team]
  
  
  # Expected goals
  lambda <- exp(baseline + home_advantage) * home_att * away_def
  mu <- exp(baseline) * away_att * home_def
  
  goals <- 0:max_goals

  # Independent Poisson scoreline probabilities
  probs <- outer(dpois(goals, lambda), dpois(goals, mu))

  # testttttt
  if (length(lambda) != 1 || length(mu) != 1 ||
    !is.finite(lambda) || !is.finite(mu) ||
    lambda <= 0 || mu <= 0) {

  print(list(
    home_team = home_team,
    away_team = away_team,
    home_att = home_att,
    home_def = home_def,
    away_att = away_att,
    away_def = away_def,
    lambda = lambda,
    mu = mu
  ))
}
  # correction
  probs[1, 1] <- probs[1, 1] * (1 - lambda * mu * rho)
  probs[1, 2] <- probs[1, 2] * (1 + lambda * rho)
  probs[2, 1] <- probs[2, 1] * (1 + mu * rho)
  probs[2, 2] <- probs[2, 2] * (1 - rho)

    # for some cases can end up with negative prob cause correction so we check 
    # for that.
  if (any(!is.finite(probs)) || any(probs < 0) ||
      !is.finite(sum(probs)) || sum(probs) <= 0) {
    stop(paste("Invalid scoreline probabilities for:",
               home_team, "vs", away_team))}

  # normalise
  probs <- probs / sum(probs)
  
  if (nrow(probs) < 2 || ncol(probs) < 2) {
    stop("Probability matrix is too small.")}
  
  return(probs)
}

```

Slightly frustratingly, the dixon coles adjuster now takes single fixtures as 
input rather than the split home and away goal data. Thus we will relabel train
data as for dixon coles at appropriate step of creation.

Now we have our function to give the dixon-coles adjusted probabilities of each
scoreline allowed by the max goals param, we will begin to use the dc adjustment
for prediction. First let us define a predictive function. We want this to give
multiple predictions: the expected number of home and away goals for initial 
validation, the probability of a home win, an away win and a draw for when we 
are predicting the a league table.

```{r Dc predictor func}
predict_dc_fixture <- function(home_team, away_team,
                               team_ratings, baseline,
                               home_advantage,
                               rho = -0.05, max_goals = 7) {

  probs <- dixon_coles_probs(
    team_ratings = team_ratings, home_team = home_team,
    away_team = away_team,baseline = baseline, home_advantage = home_advantage,
    rho = rho, max_goals = max_goals)

  # expected goals under model used in model validation
  goals <- 0:(nrow(probs) - 1)

  expected_home_goals <- sum(rowSums(probs) * goals)
  expected_away_goals <- sum(colSums(probs) * goals)

  # the prob of a match outcome (used later for league table)
  prob_home_win <- sum(probs[row(probs) > col(probs)])
  prob_draw <- sum(probs[row(probs) == col(probs)])
  prob_away_win <- sum(probs[row(probs) < col(probs)])

  data.frame(
    expected_home_goals = expected_home_goals,
    expected_away_goals = expected_away_goals, prob_home_win = prob_home_win,
    prob_draw = prob_draw, prob_away_win = prob_away_win)}
```

Now we can see how the dc model fares on it's validation data.

This table shows that the Dixon-Coles adjustment with rho = -0.05 has shown no 
improvement on our prediction of the goals scored in our validation data. This 
is not overly suprising since the adjustment is not neccersarily designed to 
improve the prediction of exact goal counts. More so, the adjustment affects the
joint scoreline distribution for scorelines (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), and (0,1).

## Rolling window validation
In our validation tests, we want to consider both our prediction of a complete season, and prediction of a season which has already began. 

We choose a season end date of July 27th and a season start date of the 28th of july. That is, each season runs from 01/08/20(yy) to 31/07/20(yy+1). For each test window, we will create two validation sets: one in which we predict the entire validation period, ie complete season prediction, and another where we predict all games after a cut-off period.

Note that we are assuming that if we can accurately model the number of goals that will be scored in a game, then we will be able to predict the table at the end of the season [COULD ADD XG PREDICTED TABLE TO SHOW THIS IS A GOOD IDEA].

First, we build our validation sets from the epl_all and ech_all data.

```{r rolling window validation window creation}

generate_validation <- function(ech_all, epl_all, year, cutoff) {
  start_date <- as.Date(paste0(year, "-07-28"))
  end_date   <- as.Date(paste0(year + 1, "-07-27"))

  # all data before the season begins
  historical_ech <- ech_all %>%
    filter(Date < start_date)

  historical_epl <- epl_all %>%
    filter(Date < start_date)

  # fixtures/results belonging to the target season
  target_ech <- ech_all %>%
    filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)

  target_epl <- epl_all %>%
    filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)

  # complete season 
  complete_season <- list(
    ech_train = historical_ech,
    epl_train = historical_epl,
    ech_test  = target_ech,
    epl_test  = target_epl)

  # in season
  cutoff <- as.Date(cutoff)

  in_season <- list(
    ech_train = ech_all %>%
      filter(Date < cutoff),
    epl_train = epl_all %>%
      filter(Date < cutoff),
    ech_test = target_ech %>%
      filter(Date >= cutoff),
    epl_test = target_epl %>%
      filter(Date >= cutoff)
  )
   

  return(list(
    complete_season = complete_season,
    in_season = in_season))
}
```

Below is a chunk testing the code to ensure all is as should be, let us generate for the year 2024, with cutoff 01/11/2023.

Okie dokie, this all seems to be behaving. We will now build our rolling validation sets. We're going to dress this up in a wrapper function for better Q.o.L.

```{r building the validation sets, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
generate_rolling_validation <- function(epl_all, ech_all, years, cutoff_month, cutoff_day) {

  rolling_window_sets <- lapply(years, function(year){
    cutoff <- as.Date(sprintf(  "%d-%02d-%02d",
      year, cutoff_month, cutoff_day))
      
    generate_validation(ech_all, epl_all, year, cutoff)
    }) 
  names(rolling_window_sets) <- years
  return(rolling_window_sets)
}
```

Perfect so we have our rolling train and test sets for both whole season prediction and for incomplete season prediction.

The first thing we will do is use these rolling window validation sets to find scalars $\alpha_{p,c}, \alpha_{c,p}, \delta_{p,c}, \delta_{c,p} $. These will act as a linear estimate for scaling attack and defence estimates between leagues. I.e  a promoted team_i attack's rating in first game of new prem season is $\alpha_i \alpha_{c,p}$. 

Also, we will give any team promoted into the championship from league 1 median championship attack and defence ratings. This is a limitation of the model, however, since we are attempting to model premier league table, we hope that we will be able to accurately adjust these ratings over the minimum course of the single championship season which it would take for a team from league one to get to the premier league. Note that any info we had about the team in seasons prior to their stint in league 1 is "forgotten".

We will now extract the promoted and relegated teams:

```{r 1} 
library(dplyr)
get_season_teams <- function(data, year) {
# again note that year is the first year of season ie 2014 gives the 2014/15 season. This is also adjusted to take the goals data or the _all data.
  start_date <- as.Date(paste0(year, "-07-28"))
  end_date   <- as.Date(paste0(year + 1, "-07-27"))

  season_data <- data %>%
    filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)

  unique(c(
    as.character(season_data$HomeTeam),
    as.character(season_data$AwayTeam)))
}
```
We now use this function to adjust the ratings in consecutive seasons as follows:

```{r 2}
# gives ratings for start of year given ratings from previous year.
adjust_division_ratings <- function(
    epl_ratings,
    ech_ratings,
    epl_all,
    ech_all,
    year,
    a_p, d_p, a_c, d_c
) {

  # all teams in season current and season previous
  current_epl <- get_season_teams(epl_all, year)
  current_ech <- get_season_teams(ech_all, year)

  previous_epl <- get_season_teams(epl_all, year - 1)
  previous_ech <- get_season_teams(ech_all, year - 1)

  # promoted and relegated sides
  promoted_to_epl <- intersect(current_epl, previous_ech)

  relegated_to_ech <- intersect(current_ech, previous_epl)

  # league 1 to champ
  new_ech_entrants <- setdiff(
    current_ech, union(previous_ech, previous_epl))

  # retreive ratings func
  get_rows <- function(teams, ratings) {
    idx <- match(teams, ratings$team_names)
    ratings[idx, , drop = FALSE]}

  # prem teams
  epl_stayers <- setdiff(current_epl, promoted_to_epl)

  epl_adjusted <- get_rows(epl_stayers, epl_ratings)

  # champ to prem teams
  promoted_ratings <- get_rows(promoted_to_epl, ech_ratings)

  promoted_ratings$att_rating <-
    promoted_ratings$att_rating * a_p

  promoted_ratings$def_rating <-
    promoted_ratings$def_rating * d_p

  epl_adjusted <- bind_rows(
    epl_adjusted, promoted_ratings)

  # champ teams
  ech_stayers <- setdiff(
    current_ech,
    c(relegated_to_ech, new_ech_entrants))

  ech_adjusted <- get_rows(ech_stayers, ech_ratings)

  # relegated to champ transfer
  relegated_ratings <- get_rows(relegated_to_ech, epl_ratings)

  relegated_ratings$att_rating <-
    relegated_ratings$att_rating * a_c

  relegated_ratings$def_rating <-
    relegated_ratings$def_rating * d_c

  ech_adjusted <- bind_rows(
    ech_adjusted, relegated_ratings)

  # new champ teams
  if (length(new_ech_entrants) > 0) {

    median_attack <- median(ech_ratings$att_rating)
    median_defence <- median(ech_ratings$def_rating)

    new_ratings <- data.frame(
      team_names = new_ech_entrants,
      att_rating = median_attack, def_rating = median_defence)

    ech_adjusted <- bind_rows(
      ech_adjusted, new_ratings)}

  # Ensure ratings follow the current season's team order
  epl_adjusted <- epl_adjusted[
    match(current_epl, epl_adjusted$team_names),]

  ech_adjusted <- ech_adjusted[
    match(current_ech, ech_adjusted$team_names),]

  return(list(
    epl_ratings = epl_adjusted,
    ech_ratings = ech_adjusted,
    promoted_to_epl = promoted_to_epl,
    relegated_to_ech = relegated_to_ech,
    new_ech_entrants = new_ech_entrants))
}


epl_ratings_adjusted <- adjusted_ratings$epl_ratings
ech_ratings_adjusted <- adjusted_ratings$ech_ratings
```

Next we need to add a function so to allow us to prepare our rolling window dfs. We will use our home away split logic and then fit our models on the training data.

```{r 3}
library(dplyr)
prepare_training_goals <- function(data, known_date, cut_off, power) {

  train_data <- data %>%
    filter(Date < known_date) %>%
    mutate(days_ago = as.numeric(known_date - Date)) %>%
    filter(days_ago < cut_off) %>%
    mutate(obvs_weight = weight(days_ago, cut_off, power))

  def_home_away_split_train(train_data)}


fit_division_models <- function(epl_train, ech_train,
    known_date, cut_off, power) {

  # Prepare goal-level training data
  train_epl_goals <- prepare_training_goals(
    epl_train, known_date, cut_off, power)

  train_ech_goals <- prepare_training_goals(
    ech_train, known_date, cut_off, power)

  # Fit separate Poisson GLMs
  epl_goal_model <- glm(
    Goals ~ Home + Team + Opponent,
    family = poisson(link = "log"),
    data = train_epl_goals,
    weights = obvs_weight)

  ech_goal_model <- glm(
    Goals ~ Home + Team + Opponent,
    family = poisson(link = "log"),
    data = train_ech_goals,
    weights = obvs_weight)

  # Extract ratings and model parameters
  epl_model <- extract_ratings(epl_goal_model)
  ech_model <- extract_ratings(ech_goal_model)

  return(list(
    epl_ratings = epl_model$ratings,
    ech_ratings = ech_model$ratings,

    epl_baseline = epl_model$baseline,
    epl_home_advantage = epl_model$home_advantage,

    ech_baseline = ech_model$baseline,
    ech_home_advantage = ech_model$home_advantage,
    
     epl_goal_model = epl_goal_model,
    ech_goal_model = ech_goal_model))}
```

Right, we're getting there now. We will make amendment to the dc evaluation model so it will work on the validation data sets.

```{r}
evaluate_dc_fixtures <- function(data, team_ratings,
    baseline, home_advantage, rho = -0.05, max_goals = 10){
  
  # Predict expected goals for every fixture
  predictions <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(data)), function(i) {

    predict_dc_fixture(home_team = data$HomeTeam[i],
      away_team = data$AwayTeam[i],
      team_ratings = team_ratings,
      baseline = baseline,
      home_advantage = home_advantage,
      rho = rho,
      max_goals = max_goals)})

  predictions <- bind_rows(predictions)

  results <- bind_cols(
    data %>% select(Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG),
    predictions
  )

  # Combine home and away observations
  actual <- c(results$FTHG, results$FTAG)

  predicted <- c(
    results$expected_home_goals,
    results$expected_away_goals
  )

  errors <- actual - predicted

  metrics <- data.frame(
    n_fixtures = nrow(data),
    n_observations = length(actual),
    mean_actual = mean(actual),
    mean_predicted = mean(predicted),
    MAE = mean(abs(errors)),
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2))
  )

  return(list(
    metrics = metrics,
    predictions = results
  ))
}
```

We are going to use a combination over equal equity of MAE and RMSE as our optimisation objective. Reiterating again that we are going to assume that an increase in the accuracy of our goal predictions will cause an increase in the accuracy of our league table by the end of the season.

We will first tune the league adjustment scalars. We will run procedure over complete season data, then again for in season data. We will aggregate the MSE and RMSE and choose the the set of scalars which result in the minimal realised values of these. 

```{r WE GOT TO HERE}
validation_mode <- "complete_season"

years <- 2015:2023

# time weight params (to be tuned seperatley later)
power <- 3
cut_off <- 730

# dc params (rho also to be tuned)
rho <- -0.05
max_goals <- 7

# we will also get the known date (note this needs to be changed if we change the season start or the in_season_cut date)

get_known_date <- function(year, mode) {

  if (mode == "complete_season") {
    return(as.Date(sprintf("%d-07-27", year)))}
  if (mode == "in_season") {
    return(as.Date(sprintf("%d-11-01", year)))}}

# also we will prefit the glm model to the data
prepare_rolling_models <- function(
    rw_validation_sets,
    years,
    mode,
    cut_off,
    power
) {

  results <- lapply(years, function(year) {

    validation <-rw_validation_sets[[as.character(year)]][[mode]]

    # Use the start of the target season as the information date
    known_date <- as.Date(paste0(year, "-07-28"))

    fitted_models <- fit_division_models(
      epl_train = validation$epl_train,
      ech_train = validation$ech_train,
      known_date = known_date,
      cut_off = cut_off,
      power = power
    )

    list(
      year = year,
      known_date = known_date,
      fitted_models = fitted_models,
      epl_test = validation$epl_test,
      ech_test = validation$ech_test
    )
  })

  names(results) <- as.character(years)

  return(results)
}


rolling_models <- prepare_rolling_models(
  rw_validation_sets = rw_validation_sets,
  years = years,
  mode = validation_mode,
  cut_off = cut_off,
  power = power)
```
Note: we can prefit the model to the data so that we don't have to run through this step for every scalar change. This is fine since the scalar change does not affect the regression coeffs.

We now make our scoring function for the dc_game model.
```{r}
score_dc_fixtures <- function(
    data,
    team_ratings,
    baseline,
    home_advantage,
    rho = -0.05,
    max_goals = 7
) {

  predictions <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(data)), function(i) {

  if (!(data$HomeTeam[i] %in% team_ratings$team_names) ||
      !(data$AwayTeam[i] %in% team_ratings$team_names)) {

    print(list(
      fixture = i,
      home_team = data$HomeTeam[i],
      away_team = data$AwayTeam[i],
      missing_home = !(data$HomeTeam[i] %in% team_ratings$team_names),
      missing_away = !(data$AwayTeam[i] %in% team_ratings$team_names)
    ))
  }

  predict_dc_fixture(
    home_team = data$HomeTeam[i],
    away_team = data$AwayTeam[i],
    team_ratings = team_ratings,
    baseline = baseline,
    home_advantage = home_advantage,
    rho = rho,
    max_goals = max_goals
  )
})

  predictions <- bind_rows(predictions)

  actual <- c(data$FTHG, data$FTAG)

  predicted <- c(
    predictions$expected_home_goals,
    predictions$expected_away_goals
  )

  errors <- actual - predicted

  return(list(
    n = length(errors),
    absolute_error_sum = sum(abs(errors)),
    squared_error_sum = sum(errors^2),
    MAE = mean(abs(errors)),
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2))
  ))
}
```
## Tuning the league transition scalars (CODE to not be ran as takes years)
(NOTE: due to the unoptimised code, this section takes years to compile. As such i will leave the code in without running it and just publish the tables.)

Okay, now we need to design a function which evaluates a set of parameter values. We will then be able to make an array of param values which we can test, choosing the best one.

```{r}
evaluate_transition_parameters <- function(
    a_p, d_p, a_c, d_c,
    rolling_models,
    epl_all,
    ech_all,
    rho = -0.05,
    max_goals = 5
) {

  yearly_results <- lapply(rolling_models, function(validation) {

    year <- validation$year
    fitted <- validation$fitted_models

    # Apply promotion/relegation adjustments
    adjusted <- adjust_division_ratings(
      epl_ratings = fitted$epl_ratings,
      ech_ratings = fitted$ech_ratings,
      epl_all = epl_all,
      ech_all = ech_all,
      year = year,
      a_p = a_p,
      d_p = d_p,
      a_c = a_c,
      d_c = d_c
    )

    # Evaluate EPL predictions
    epl_score <- score_dc_fixtures(
      data = validation$epl_test,
      team_ratings = adjusted$epl_ratings,
      baseline = fitted$epl_baseline,
      home_advantage = fitted$epl_home_advantage,
      rho = rho,
      max_goals = max_goals
    )

    # Evaluate Championship predictions
    ech_score <- score_dc_fixtures(
      data = validation$ech_test,
      team_ratings = adjusted$ech_ratings,
      baseline = fitted$ech_baseline,
      home_advantage = fitted$ech_home_advantage,
      rho = rho,
      max_goals = max_goals
    )

    # Combine the two divisions
    total_n <- epl_score$n + ech_score$n

    total_abs <- epl_score$absolute_error_sum +
      ech_score$absolute_error_sum

    total_sq <- epl_score$squared_error_sum +
      ech_score$squared_error_sum

    data.frame(
      year = year,
      EPL_MAE = epl_score$MAE,
      EPL_RMSE = epl_score$RMSE,
      ECH_MAE = ech_score$MAE,
      ECH_RMSE = ech_score$RMSE,
      Combined_MAE = total_abs / total_n,
      Combined_RMSE = sqrt(total_sq / total_n),
      n_observations = total_n,
      absolute_error_sum = total_abs,
      squared_error_sum = total_sq
    )
  })

  yearly_results <- bind_rows(yearly_results)

  # Overall results
  total_n <- sum(yearly_results$n_observations)
  total_abs <- sum(yearly_results$absolute_error_sum)
  total_sq <- sum(yearly_results$squared_error_sum)

  summary <- data.frame(
    a_p = a_p,
    d_p = d_p,
    a_c = a_c,
    d_c = d_c,

    Mean_EPL_MAE = mean(yearly_results$EPL_MAE),
    Mean_ECH_MAE = mean(yearly_results$ECH_MAE),

    Mean_Combined_MAE = mean(yearly_results$Combined_MAE),

    Pooled_Combined_MAE = total_abs / total_n,
    Pooled_Combined_RMSE = sqrt(total_sq / total_n),

    SD_Combined_MAE = sd(yearly_results$Combined_MAE)
  )

  return(list(
    summary = summary,
    yearly_results = yearly_results
  ))
}
```

Our parameter grid below:
(note this grid is very coarse. we may be able to refine this later given a ball park) Also since this is computationally murderous in the current setup (apologies), im going to impose that champ team ratings can only get worse going to prem. I will make no restriction on prem to champ since back to back relegations are not unheard of haowever back to back top finishes over leagues is uncommon.

```{r}
parameter_grid <- expand.grid(
  a_p = c(0.8,0.9,1.0),
  d_p = c(1.0, 1.1, 1.2),
  a_c = c(0.8,1.0,1.2),
  d_c = c(0.8, 1.0,1.2))
```

Now we run the experiment.


# Tuning power and cut_off

For ease we will use a rho value of -0.13 as found in the blog https://opisthokonta.net/?p=890. We may look to find our own parameter value if the time constraints allow, but for now this will suffice. We do, however, need to tune the power and cut_off parameters for our time weighting functions. We will use a coarse grid initially for this which we may refine if time allows.

```{r power_cutoff grid}
power_grid <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4)

cut_off_grid <- c(365, 730, 1095, 1460,1825, 2190, 2555)

weighting_grid <- expand.grid(power= power_grid, cutoff = cut_off_grid)
```
Now we rerun our tuning experiment with other parameters fixed.

```{r weight tuner}
weighting_results <- vector("list", nrow(weighting_grid))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(weighting_grid))) {

  current_power <- weighting_grid$power[i]
  current_cut_off <- weighting_grid$cut_off[i]

  cat(
    "\nCombination", i, "of", nrow(weighting_grid),
    "| Power:", current_power,
    "| Cut-off:", current_cut_off, "days\n"
  )

  rolling_models <- prepare_rolling_models(
    rw_validation_sets = rw_validation_sets,
    years = years,
    mode = "complete_season",
    cut_off = current_cut_off,
    power = current_power
  )

  result <- evaluate_transition_parameters(
    a_p = 0.7,
    d_p = 1.2,
    a_c = 1.4,
    d_c = 0.6,
    rolling_models = rolling_models,
    epl_all = epl_all,
    ech_all = ech_all,
    rho = -0.13,
    max_goals = 7
  )

  weighting_results[[i]] <- result

  cat("Combined MAE:",
    round(result$summary$Pooled_Combined_MAE, 5),"\n")
}

weighting_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_along(weighting_results), function(i) {

    cbind(
      power = weighting_grid$power[i],
      cut_off = weighting_grid$cut_off[i],
      weighting_results[[i]]$summary
    )

  })
) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Pooled_Combined_MAE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Rank = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Rank,
    power,
    cut_off,
    Mean_EPL_MAE,
    Mean_ECH_MAE,
    Pooled_Combined_MAE,
    Pooled_Combined_RMSE,
    SD_Combined_MAE
  )

head(weighting_summary)
```

Our lowest combined MAE is given when we use power = 0.5 and cut_off = 2555. If we plot this weighting curve it gives:

```{r}
power <- 0.5
cut_off <- 2555

weighting_data <- data.frame(
  days_ago = seq(0, cut_off, length.out = 1000)
) %>%
  mutate(
    weight = ifelse(
      days_ago >= cut_off,
      0,
      1 - (days_ago / cut_off)^power
    )
  )

ggplot(weighting_data, aes(x = days_ago, y = weight)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Historical Observation Weighting Function",
    subtitle = "Power = 0.5 | Cut-off = 2555 days",
    x = "Age of observation (days)",
    y = "Observation weight"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_classic()
```

This is contrary to my prior that the best weighting curve would be concave. We will use these parameters in our final model.

```{r predicting table function}
predict_fixtures <- function(
    fixtures,
    team_ratings,
    baseline,
    home_advantage,
    rho = -0.13,
    max_goals = 7) {

  results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(fixtures)), function(i) {

    home <- fixtures$HomeTeam[i]
    away <- fixtures$AwayTeam[i]

    probs <- dixon_coles_probs(
      team_ratings = team_ratings,
      home_team = home,
      away_team = away,
      baseline = baseline,
      home_advantage = home_advantage,
      rho = rho,
      max_goals = max_goals)

    goals <- 0:max_goals

    expected_home <- sum(probs * matrix(
      goals,
      nrow = length(goals),
      ncol = length(goals)))

    expected_away <- sum(probs * matrix(
      goals,
      nrow = length(goals),
      ncol = length(goals),
      byrow = TRUE))

    home_win <- sum(probs[row(probs) > col(probs)])
    draw <- sum(diag(probs))
    away_win <- sum(probs[row(probs) < col(probs)])

    most_likely <- which(
      probs == max(probs), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]

    data.frame(
      Date = fixtures$Date[i],
      HomeTeam = home,
      AwayTeam = away,
      Expected_Home_Goals = expected_home,
      Expected_Away_Goals = expected_away,
      Predicted_Score = paste0(
        most_likely[1] - 1, "-",
        most_likely[2] - 1),
      Home_Win_Prob = home_win,
      Draw_Prob = draw,
      Away_Win_Prob = away_win,
      Expected_Home_Points = 3 * home_win + draw,
      Expected_Away_Points = 3 * away_win + draw)})

  dplyr::bind_rows(results)
}
```


```{r making predictions}
epl_predictions <- predict_fixtures(
  epl_test,
  final_ratings$epl_ratings,
  final_models$epl_baseline,
  final_models$epl_home_advantage)

ech_predictions <- predict_fixtures(
  ech_test,
  final_ratings$ech_ratings,
  final_models$ech_baseline,
  final_models$ech_home_advantage)
```

```{r building function to create league table}
compare_league_tables <- function(fixtures, predictions) {

  # Predicted home-team contributions
  predicted_home <- data.frame(
    Team = predictions$HomeTeam,
    P = 1,
    Expected_Pts = predictions$Expected_Home_Points,
    Expected_GF = predictions$Expected_Home_Goals,
    Expected_GA = predictions$Expected_Away_Goals)

  # Predicted away-team contributions
  predicted_away <- data.frame(
    Team = predictions$AwayTeam,
    P = 1,
    Expected_Pts = predictions$Expected_Away_Points,
    Expected_GF = predictions$Expected_Away_Goals,
    Expected_GA = predictions$Expected_Home_Goals)

  predicted_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    predicted_home, predicted_away) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Team) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      P = sum(P),
      Expected_Pts = sum(Expected_Pts),
      Expected_GF = sum(Expected_GF),
      Expected_GA = sum(Expected_GA),
      Expected_GD = Expected_GF - Expected_GA,
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      dplyr::desc(Expected_Pts),
      dplyr::desc(Expected_GD),
      dplyr::desc(Expected_GF)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Predicted_Rank = dplyr::row_number())

  # Actual results: exclude any fixtures without a final score
  completed <- fixtures %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(FTHG), !is.na(FTAG))

  actual_home <- data.frame(
    Team = completed$HomeTeam,
    GF = completed$FTHG,
    GA = completed$FTAG
  )

  actual_away <- data.frame(
    Team = completed$AwayTeam,
    GF = completed$FTAG,
    GA = completed$FTHG
  )

  actual_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    actual_home, actual_away
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      W = as.integer(GF > GA),
      D = as.integer(GF == GA),
      L = as.integer(GF < GA),
      Pts = 3 * W + D
    )

  actual_table <- actual_results %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Team) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      P = dplyr::n(),
      W = sum(W),
      D = sum(D),
      L = sum(L),
      GF = sum(GF),
      GA = sum(GA),
      GD = GF - GA,
      Pts = sum(Pts),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      dplyr::desc(Pts),
      dplyr::desc(GD),
      dplyr::desc(GF)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Actual_Rank = dplyr::row_number())

  # Join predicted and actual positions
  comparison <- dplyr::full_join(
    predicted_table,
    actual_table,
    by = "Team",
    suffix = c("_Predicted", "_Actual")
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Rank_Difference = Predicted_Rank - Actual_Rank
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Actual_Rank)

  return(list(comparison = comparison))
}
```

```{r creating league table}
epl_tables <- compare_league_tables(
  fixtures = epl_test,
  predictions = epl_predictions
)

ech_tables <- compare_league_tables(
  fixtures = ech_test,
  predictions = ech_predictions
)
```

```{r creating final prediction output df}

epl_prediction <- epl_tables$comparison%>%
  select(Team, Actual_Rank, Predicted_Rank, Rank_Difference,
         Expected_Pts, Pts)
  
epl_prediction

ech_prediction <- ech_tables$comparison%>%
  select(Team, Actual_Rank, Predicted_Rank, Rank_Difference,
         Expected_Pts, Pts)
  
ech_prediction

```

Okie dokie we have our predicted tables for the 25-26 seasons. As we can see, they are moderately unsuccessful. I think a big issue is that we are assuming that past performance is indicative of future results which is not always the case.
